author: Thomas à Kempis
title: Of the proving of the true lover

verses.text: “My Son, thou art not yet strong and prudent in thy love.”
verses.modernizedText: “My Son, you are not yet strong and prudent in your love.”

verses.text: Wherefore, O my Lord?
verses.modernizedText: Why, O my Lord?

verses.text: “Because for a little opposition thou fallest away from thy undertakings, and too eagerly seekest after consolation.
verses.modernizedText: “Because at a little opposition you fall away from your undertakings, and seek consolation too eagerly.

verses.text: The strong lover standeth fast in temptations, and believeth not the evil persuasions of the enemy.
verses.modernizedText: The strong lover stands fast in temptations and does not believe the evil persuasions of the enemy.

verses.text: As in prosperity I please him, so in adversity I do not displease.
verses.modernizedText: As I please him in prosperity, so I do not displease him in adversity.

verses.text: “The prudent lover considereth not the gift of the lover so much as the love of the giver.
verses.modernizedText: “The prudent lover considers not so much the gift of the lover as the love of the giver.

verses.text: He looketh for the affection more than the value, and setteth all gifts lower than the Beloved.
verses.modernizedText: He looks for the affection more than the value, and sets all gifts below the Beloved.

verses.text: The noble lover resteth not in the gift, but in Me above every gift.
verses.modernizedText: The noble lover does not rest in the gift, but in Me above every gift.

verses.text: “All is not lost, though thou sometimes think of Me or of My saints, less than thou shouldest desire.
verses.modernizedText: “All is not lost, though you sometimes think of Me or of My saints less than you would desire.

verses.text: That good and sweet affection which thou sometimes perceivest is the effect of present grace and some foretaste of the heavenly country; but hereon thou must not too much depend, for it goeth and cometh.
verses.modernizedText: That good and sweet affection which you sometimes perceive is the effect of present grace and some foretaste of the heavenly country; but you must not depend too much on it, for it comes and goes.

verses.text: But to strive against the evil motions of the mind which come to us, and to resist the suggestions of the devil, is a token of virtue and great merit.
verses.modernizedText: But to strive against the evil motions of the mind that come to us, and to resist the suggestions of the devil, is a token of virtue and great merit.

verses.text: “Therefore let not strange fancies disturb thee, whencesoever they arise.
verses.modernizedText: “Therefore do not let strange fancies disturb you, wherever they arise.

verses.text: Bravely observe thy purpose and thy upright intentions towards God.
verses.modernizedText: Bravely hold to your purpose and your upright intentions toward God.

verses.text: It is not an illusion when thou art sometimes suddenly carried away into rapture, and then suddenly art brought back to the wonted vanities of thy heart.
verses.modernizedText: It is not an illusion when you are sometimes suddenly carried away into rapture, and then suddenly brought back to the usual vanities of your heart.

verses.text: For thou dost rather unwillingly undergo them than cause them; and so long as they displease thee and thou strivest against them, it is a merit and no loss.
verses.modernizedText: For you undergo them unwillingly rather than cause them; and as long as they displease you and you strive against them, it is a merit and no loss.

verses.text: “Know thou that thine old enemy altogether striveth to hinder thy pursuit after good, and to deter thee from every godly exercise, to wit, the contemplation of the Saints, the pious remembrance of My passion, the profitable recollection of sin, the keeping of thy own heart, and the steadfast purpose to grow in virtue.
verses.modernizedText: “Know that your old enemy strives altogether to hinder your pursuit of good, and to deter you from every godly exercise: the contemplation of the Saints, the pious remembrance of My passion, the profitable recollection of sin, the keeping of your own heart, and the steadfast purpose to grow in virtue.

verses.text: He suggesteth to thee many evil thoughts, that he may work in thee weariness and terror, and so draw thee away from prayer and holy reading.
verses.modernizedText: He suggests many evil thoughts to you, that he may produce weariness and terror in you, and so draw you away from prayer and holy reading.

verses.text: Humble confession displeaseth him, and if he were able he would make thee to cease from Communion.
verses.modernizedText: Humble confession displeases him, and if he were able he would make you cease from Communion.

verses.text: Believe him not, nor heed him, though many a time he hath laid for thee the snares of deceit.
verses.modernizedText: Do not believe him or heed him, though many a time he has laid snares of deceit for you.

verses.text: Account it to be from him, when he suggesteth evil and unclean thoughts.
verses.modernizedText: Consider it to be from him when he suggests evil and unclean thoughts.

verses.text: Say unto him, ‘Depart unclean spirit; put on shame, miserable one; horribly unclean art thou, who bringest such things to mine ears.
verses.modernizedText: Say to him, ‘Depart, unclean spirit; put on shame, miserable one; horribly unclean are you, who bring such things to my ears.

verses.text: Depart from me, detestable deceiver; thou shalt have no part in me; but Jesus shall be with me, as a strong warrior, and thou shalt stand confounded.
verses.modernizedText: Depart from me, detestable deceiver; you will have no part in me; but Jesus will be with me as a strong warrior, and you will stand confounded.

verses.text: Rather would I die and bear all suffering, than consent unto thee.
verses.modernizedText: I would rather die and bear all suffering than consent to you.

verses.text: Hold thy peace and be dumb; I will not hear thee more, though thou plottest more snares against me.
verses.modernizedText: Be silent and be dumb; I will not hear you any more, though you plot more snares against me.

verses.text: The Lord is my light and my salvation: whom then shall I fear?
verses.modernizedText: The Lord is my light and my salvation: whom then shall I fear?

verses.text: Though a host of men should rise up against me, yet shall not my heart be afraid.
verses.modernizedText: Though a host of men should rise up against me, yet my heart will not be afraid.

verses.text: The Lord is my strength and my Redeemer.’(1)
verses.modernizedText: The Lord is my strength and my Redeemer.’(1)

verses.text: “Strive thou like a good soldier; and if sometimes thou fail through weakness, put on thy strength more bravely than before, trusting in My more abundant grace, and take thou much heed of vain confidence and pride.
verses.modernizedText: “Strive like a good soldier; and if you sometimes fail through weakness, put on your strength more bravely than before, trusting in My more abundant grace, and take great care against vain confidence and pride.

verses.text: Because of it many are led into error, and sometimes fall into blindness well-nigh irremediable.
verses.modernizedText: Because of it many are led into error, and sometimes fall into blindness that is nearly beyond remedy.

verses.text: Let this ruin of the proud, who foolishly lift themselves up, be to thee for a warning and a continual exhortation to humility.”
verses.modernizedText: Let this ruin of the proud, who foolishly lift themselves up, be a warning to you and a continual exhortation to humility.”
